1) Scenario (production-shaped)

Checkout chain under load. Inventory stock lookup runs a CPU ledger scan (WAREHOUSE_LEDGER + checksum) instead of an indexed hit — still returns HTTP 200. Callers wait; no 5xx. From Datadog’s point of view this is a latency / response-time problem across three services — not an error-rate Incident.

Trace tree — SLOWDOWN leaf
FEGET /api/checkout → 200 ~9–22s status:ok
ProductGET /api/product → 200 ~9–22s status:ok
LeafGET /api/stock → 200 ~9–22s

Leaf = longest self-time on inventory (CPU) — not an error status.

2) What the app emits (all three rails)

Metrics

APM auto: trace.flask.request duration / hits (errors stay ~0).
Host: CPU user% rises with the slow window (Bits: sustained ~52–57% on DESKTOP-MBPAQK1).

Traces

ddtrace FE→product→inventory. All status:ok / HTTP 200. Leaf span inventory.stock holds wall time; flask.jsonify is trivial after the scan.

Logs

JSON ok path: event:inventory.stock.ok, http_status:200, sku, dd.trace_id. 0 KeyError — contrast the ERROR run.

Unified Service Tags stamp service / env / version on every rail. APM lowercases version tags — join carefully with logs’ mixed-case stamp.

3) How each rail sees this slowdown

3.1 Metrics rail

Latency is a duration series, not an error count. p95:trace.flask.request{service:inventory,…} jumps from ~5 ms baseline to ~9–22 s. Host CPU confirms CPU-bound work. Error-rate series stay quiet — Door A Flask High Error Rate misses this category.
SeriesHealthyFaultUsed by

Host CPU user%~8–10%~52–57%Infra corroboration (Bits)
trace.flask.request.errors/hits~0~0Error Door A stays OK

3.2 Traces (APM) rail

Spans are ground truth for where time is spent. Resource-level durations look equal across services; only the deepest inventory.stock span is self-time. Sort by @duration, not status:error.

3.3 Logs rail

Logs corroborate success path — they do not scream ERROR. Join via dd.trace_id to the slow flamegraph; expect inventory.stock.ok.

5) Correlate one request (M∥T∥L)

  1. Metrics — see p95 / CPU rise for inventory (and callers’ wall time).
  2. Traces — open a slow ok trace; read deepest self-time span (inventory.stock).
  3. Logs — same dd.trace_id → inventory.stock.ok / 200 (not KeyError).
  4. Related — keep env:rca-lab-e3 + fault window constant.
Do not stop at “all three services are slow.” Equal resource duration is the wait cascade; the leaf is inventory self-time.

Teaching point: error-rate Detect ≠ latency Detect. Strong MTL still does not auto-open Watchdog or Incident.

7) Flamegraph leaf (operator RCA)

  1. Filter ok spans with @duration:>5s (not status:error).
  2. Open a slow checkout trace.
  3. Select the longest self-time leaf (inventory.stock), not the equal-duration parent resources.
  4. Confirm with host CPU and ok logs.

Write ≠ Detect ≠ Localize. These MCP counts are stage 03 Write evidence. Stage 05 Detect stayed empty (no latency Door A · error Door OK · Watchdog 0). The leaf was named because the lab opened APM for the known window — not because Datadog foghorned. Full insight: Timeline §2.
